* [TritonToStructured](fix) Relax LoadBroadcastConverter for different-axis ptr/mask broadcast

Previously LoadBroadcastConverter required ptr and mask broadcast source shapes to match exactly. When ptr and mask broadcast on different axes (e.g. ptr on dim0: [1,64] -> [256,64], mask on dim1: [256,1] -> [256,64]), the pattern failed to match, causing the load to fall through to MemOpConverter's PtrAnalysis path which could lose mask information and trigger an inefficient scf.for fallback in TritonToUnstructure.

Now supports two cases depending on whether the broadcast source shapes match:

Case 1 (shapes match, original fast path):
  %ptr_b = tt.broadcast %ptr_src
  %mask_b = tt.broadcast %mask_src
  %v = tt.load %ptr_b, %mask_b, %other_splat
becomes:
  %v_small = tt.load %ptr_src, %mask_src, %other_small
  %v = tt.broadcast %v_small

Case 2 (shapes differ, e.g. ptr and mask broadcast on different axes):
  %ptr_b  = tt.broadcast %ptr_src
  %mask_b = tt.broadcast %mask_src
  %v = tt.load %ptr_b, %mask_b, %other
becomes:
  %v_small = tt.load %ptr_src              (no mask/no other - safe)
  %v_bc    = tt.broadcast %v_small
  %v       = arith.select %mask_b, %v_bc, %other

The small load in case 2 does not need a mask because in ptr's non-broadcast dimensions the mask is guaranteed to be all-true, and in ptr's broadcast dimensions only one element is loaded (no OOB risk). The full mask is applied via select after broadcast; downstream Select Analysis lowers this to extract_slice / insert_slice.

Also fixes the default masked-off value from tensor.empty (poison) to a zero splat constant, matching Triton's de-facto behavior.

* [TritonToStructured](feat) Add StoreBroadcastConverter to sink stores before broadcasts

When store.ptr is defined by a `tt.broadcast`, every pointer along a broadcast axis points to the same memory address, so storing only at the first index of each broadcast axis is sufficient.

This commit adds `StoreBroadcastConverter` which:
- Rewrites stores whose ptr comes from a broadcast to use the broadcast source (smaller-shaped) ptr instead.
- Slices the value tensor along broadcast axes via `tensor::ExtractSliceOp`.
- Handles mask analogously: reuses the mask's broadcast source when available, otherwise slices the full-shaped mask.
- Includes unit tests for broadcast axis 0/1, with and without mask, and a negative test ensuring non-broadcast stores are left unchanged.

+    %base_tensor = tt.splat %base : !tt.ptr<f32> -> tensor<2x1x!tt.ptr<f32>>
+    %row_ptrs = tt.addptr %base_tensor, %row_offsets : tensor<2x1x!tt.ptr<f32>>, tensor<2x1xi64>
+    %broadcast = tt.broadcast %row_ptrs : tensor<2x1x!tt.ptr<f32>> -> tensor<2x32x!tt.ptr<f32>>
+    %range = tt.make_range {end = 32 : i32, start = 0 : i32} : tensor<32xi32>
+    %columns = tt.expand_dims %range {axis = 0 : i32} : tensor<32xi32> -> tensor<1x32xi32>
+    %column_offsets = tt.broadcast %columns : tensor<1x32xi32> -> tensor<2x32xi32>

[backend](fix) defer arch-dependent queries out of import time (#2238)

HardwareConstraints and TileGenerator read `target.arch` /
`num_vector_core` / `ub_size_in_kbytes` at class-body and module
import time, which forces device initialization as soon as the runtime
module is imported.

- hardware_consts: replace the class-body `if target.arch...` overrides
  with `field(default_factory=...)` calling `_arch_default`, evaluated
  only when an argument is omitted. Explicit values still win.
- tile_generator: snapshot `num_vector_core` on the instance and read
  the other device-dependent sizes through the `utils` module at
  construction time instead of binding them at import.
